Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

here adverb

to this place

also to here

classical

Plaut. Men. 432: eho Messēniō, accēde hūc.
Ter. Ad. 970: ehō, accēde hūc ad mē

hūc

adverb

to here

With verbs of motion: “come here” is accēde hūc, venī hūc, not hīc.

Other words

  • hōrsum — this way, hither

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 450: hōrsum pergunt

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    From hōc vorsum (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • eho Messēniō, accēde hūc. — Quid negōtī est?

    Hey, Messenio, come here. — What’s the matter?Plaut. Men. 432–432b

  • Ostende hūc manūs. — Em tibi, ostendī, eccās.

    Show me your hands. — There you are, I’ve shown them: here they are.Plaut. Aul. 640b–641

  • Manum sinistram hūc pōne.

    Put your left hand here.composed

See also here, there, where to, this way.
